description: Email: parks@buncombecounty.orgPhone: (828) 250-4260Notice - Description: Information about Open and Closed ParksMany Buncombe County Parks were impacted by Hurricane Helene.  While we are working diligently reopen parks as quickly as we can, some parks continue to remain closed. Please see the list below for which parks are open and which parks continue to be closed for safety reasons.OPEN Parks:  Lake Julian Park (please note, some disc golf holes remain closed), Hominy Valley Park, Collier Cove Nature Preserve, North Buncombe Fields, Cane Creek Playground, Buncombe County Sports Park, Corcoran Paige River Park, Bent Creek River Park, Ledges Whitewater Park, and Hominy Creek River Park.  If people choose to recreate on the river, we strongly encourage them to be aware of changes on streambanks and in the riverbed and the potential for unknown debris from Helene.CLOSED Parks:  Charles D. Owen Park, Karpen Soccer Field, Alexander River Park, Walnut Island River Park, and Glen Bridge River Park*. *Note, if the gate is open at Glen Bridge River Park, it may be used.  For safety reasons, we ask the public not to enter closed parks.Please email parks@buncombecounty.org or call (828) 250-4260 with any questions or for additional information.

title: COMING SEPTEMBER 23rd | Morgan Wade w/ Susto
location: Sierra Nevada Mills River, 100 Sierra Nevada Way, Mills River, NC, 28732
description:
Wednesday, September 23 | 6:30 PM – 10:00 PM | Amphitheater Stage | From $36.92 Event Details and Tickets 
Country singer-songwriter Morgan Wade has built a growing fan base through her raw lyrics, distinctive voice, and deeply personal music. In recent years, she has also made headlines for her high-profile friendships, fitness journey, and candid discussions about her personal life. 
Rather than smoothing over life’s rough edges, Morgan Wade leans directly into them. Never one to mince words or play coy, the celebrated singer-songwriter has built her career around undeniable honesty and vulnerable storytelling, turning life’s hardest moments into songs that feel both deeply personal and universally understood. With a voice that carries equal parts grit, vulnerability, and strength, Wade has emerged as one of the most compelling storytellers in contemporary country and roots music. 
  
Justin Osborne has been performing as ‘Susto’ since 2013, when he formed a collective of fellow musicians and artists in coastal Charleston, South Carolina. Now a bona fide emissary of alt rock and treasure to the indie crowd, a lifelong calling coupled with a cosmic push of serendipitous happenstance led to his latest venture: ‘Susto Stringband’ joined by Americana vocalist Clint Roberts, mandolinist Jackson Grimm, clawhammer banjoist Helena Rose, and upright bassist Joey Brown (now Holler Choir). 
Sierra Nevada Brewing Co. is one of America’s premier craft breweries, highly regarded for using only the finest quality ingredients.  Sierra Nevada has set the standard for craft brewers worldwide with innovations in the brewhouse as well as advances in sustainability. The view from our tree-lined brewery is something special no matter the season. Tour the brewhouse, feast in the Taproom or soak in the sun on our Back Porch with a beer, including the legendary Pale Ale and a snack. For our upcoming event line-up click here!

description:

Release and reset with a heart-centered sound bath layered with crystal beds, a pyramid, crystal light chakra balancing and energy healing!

Experience a unique and transformative sound bath journey and more! In this deeply nurturing and restorative sound bath, you will receive the additional healing benefits of lying on a full-length cushioned bed of infused amethyst crystals, with the option of lying inside our crystal-filled heart chakra pyramid or under the infused chakra balancing crystal lights. The space is anchored with many crystals, plants and a heart-centered energy that is both nurturing and magical. Group size is small so that each person can start their journey by experiencing the cleansing energy of standing inside a Tibetan foot bowl while its being played. There is nothing you have to do or prepare for, just come as you are and experience a variety of crystal and Tibetan bowls, rain sticks, bells, chimes, gongs and more while bathing in the healing energy all around you.

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

title: The Science of Happiness: The Four Noble Truths
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
The Science of Happiness: The Four Noble Truths with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

**Sundays 8/16-9/13, 10:30am-11:45am**
Whether it’s everyday stress, sadness, or even anger, our suffering can be transformed into inner strength, love, and joy. The first step is understanding its source. In this series, we’ll explore Buddha’s teachings on the Four Noble Truths. The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddhist thought and gives us a clear, precise way to understand our life and how to move forward in it. Through teachings and meditation, we’ll discover that suffering comes not from external conditions, but from our own mind. Recognizing this opens the door to transforming our experience and uncovering a more lasting, genuine happiness.
Cost: $12 (free and online options for members)

Goombay Festival returns to Asheville’s historic East End for a vibrant celebration of Black culture, music, food, art, and community! description:
Awakening Asheville
Hosted by Tish Sjoberg

2nd and 4th Sundays

Now On-Line during Covid-19 Quarantine
10:00 a.m. – 12:15 p.m.
$0 - $25 (Included in our monthly pass)

Slow down and be with yourself through art making. A rich morning that feeds your spirit, rests your body, quiets your mind and helps you remember who you are!

Here we will use the arts to have a conversation with ourselves and connect to our longings and gifts. This is not about religion, yet in the inquiry you may choose to make connections to your religious beliefs.

The format: We check in as a group, we may do a little drumming, have 5 minutes of quiet/reflection/meditation/prayer/relaxation time, go create art in silence (without talking) doing our own thing and then come back together to honor what we spent our time doing.

Art making can be painting, writing, sand tray, collage, doodling, scribbling, sewing, mixed media, movement, or…. No previous art experience necessary just the willingness to follow what you are attracted to and moving slow and quiet.

You're invited to the best play date of the year.

title: AmiciMusic presents "TRAGIC TRIOS" A Musical Commemoration of the 25th Anniversary of 9/11
location: St. Giles Chapel at Deerfield Retirement Community, 1617 Hendersonville Rd., Asheville, NC, 28803, United States
description:
Join us for this somber, but powerful tribute on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 tragedy.  Violinist Frances Hsieh (from Charleston) and cellist Franklin Keel (from Asheville) will join me to perform two incredible Piano Trios that were composed at times of immense tragedy.  Dmitri Shostakovich started his Second Piano Trio in 1943 after finding out about the death of his good friend, Ivan Solletinsky.  As news spread about the Concentration Camps in Germany, Shostakovich expanded the work to include Jewish themes and the Trio turned into an incredibly powerful tribute to the Holocaust victims and a despairing look at humanity.  Bedrich Smetana’s Piano Trio in G Minor was composed shortly after two of his young girls had passed away.  Smetana pours his grief into this amazing Trio that highlights human suffering, but also the will to keep living even in the face of unimaginable horror. 
Pianist/Artistic Director Daniel Weiser is joined by violinist Frances Hsieh from Charleston and cellist Franklin Keel from Asheville to perform two poignant Piano Trios. Dr. Weiser will talk about both pieces before they are performed and they will have their patented PianoCam so that everyone in the audience can see the keyboard. Event Details and Tickets 
  
 
 
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
AmiciMusic is a chamber music organization, dedicated to performing the highest quality chamber music in intimate venues and non-traditional spaces. We are committed to breaking down barriers between performers and audiences by setting up a more relaxed and informal atmosphere at concerts and through informative talks about each composer’s life before each piece is played. amicimusic.org

description:
Michelangelo – Love and Death offers a cinematic
journey through the great chapels and museums
of Florence, Rome and the Vatican, to the print
and drawing rooms of Europe, to explore
Michelangelo’s tempestuous life. The film goes in
search of a greater understanding of this
charismatic and enigmatic figure, both through
his relationships with his contemporaries and
his ongoing artistic legacy.
The film invites audiences to intimately examine
Michelangelo’s art and artistic process – from the
Carrara quarries where Michelangelo sourced his
marble, to the new technology being used to
attribute works. The film also offers a rare
chance to get up close to the mesmerizing
Rothschild Bronzes, which, following an
extensive research project carried out by
Academics in Cambridge in 2015, were positively
attributed to Michelangelo after over a century of debate.

title: Sep 13th Queer Platonic Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
**[REGISTER HERE](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/sep-13th-4-7pm-queer-platonic-cuddles-tranzmission-benefit)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/sep-13th-4-7pm-queer-platonic-cuddles-tranzmission-benefit)(rsvp's on Meetup do not count as registering)
This event is a fundraiser for Tranzmission. 100% of ticket sales go directly to them!

This is an event for Adults who identify as LGBTQIA+.
The intention of this event is to build community and provide a supportive place for participants to explore sweet platonic physical touch.
No one turned away for lack of funds (please ask if you truly need a scholarship or work trade).
**This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch.** We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

Consent and respect are at the forefront of the experience. We strive for a safe and welcoming environment, fostering a sense of trust that allows attendees to fully enjoy shared touch without any pressure or expectations.

Discover the joy of shared vulnerability in an environment where your authenticity is not just accepted but celebrated. This event is an opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals who appreciate the simplicity of human touch and the profound impact it can have on our well-being.

Express yourself in a way that feels true to you, whether through cozy attire or a touch of personal flair. We encourage individuality and self-expression, creating an inclusive space where everyone can be their authentic selves. Dress code is Casual and cozy.

This event will be indoors. Masks are optional. DO NOT ATTEND if you or someone you are physically close with is sick.

This is an inclusive environment where we will aim to foster the dismantling of and no tolerance of ableism, fat-shaming, homophobia/transphobia, sexism, xenophobia, classism, racism & other ideas that lead to folks feeling disconnected or unwelcome.

**THE RULES**
1\. Pants stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must ask permission and receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\. Please be specific in your requests\.
4\. If you feel a yes\, say YES\. If you feel a no\, say NO\. If you’re a maybe\, say NO\. You can always change your mind\.
5\. Get your facilitator if you have a question or concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. Talking\, laughter\, silence\, silliness\, stillness\, and crying are welcome\.

**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle.
* Please be free of strong scents; many folks would rather not be close to someone who smells of perfume, essential oils, or cigarettes
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share. The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

We take individual and group safety seriously! if you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at a touch based event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: UnRavel yo’self at Lower Big Hungry Falls
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
I am going to unravel my stress at Lower Big Hungry Falls. There is a large sand beach that is popular in warm weather. ***Bring gloves. Bring 1 small grocery bag for litter pick-up..***
**Optional:** swimming. **Bring an inner tube float.**
Remember . **Water sprites are mischievous in the Summer.**
We will spend up to 2 hrs at the Falls. Come prepared to meditate, practice your Tai-Chi, **森林浴**, read a book, prepare a meal, play a flute.
Difficulty: Natural trail w/ rock & roots & 1 short steep section.
**We are the Sloth Hiking Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !!**
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VqhCQZaH4Vs**
**This is a designated ‘silent’ Relaxation Hike; we will engage quiet for the day. But "Ooh's and Aah's" are encouraged.**
I will spend (up to) 2 hours at the falls swimming, eating, reading, ponderin’ and pretending to meditate. (shorter durations optional)
**Optional: Pack yo’ lite-weight campchair.**
**We are also doing lite clean-up maintenance.**
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair. Obstreperous raucous yawping is discouraged.
**Hike Details:**
**(Social ‘hour’ at 9:45AM. Tires roll at 10:00AM**
Length: 1.1 mi RT (in&out); **Total descent: 325 ft (and return)**
**Drive time: 20 min**
**Return Apprx: 2:30 PM**
**Carpool contributions appreciated. $2.00 suggested**
**THIS IS A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** This event is NOT for those who are uncomfortable with the antics of fun-loving dogs. Well trained dogs (you don’t have to yell.) can be 'off-leash'. Small (lap)dogs may carpool. Large dogs will drive themselves.
Weather Check: Hendersonville
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
(I currently have 2.5 driver(s). (=10)
We suggest masks and open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
**UnRuffle/UnRavel:** To experience a time of quiet in a manner that you feel worthwhile. Démêlez votre stress.
Engage the 5 senses (sight, smell, touch, taste, hearing),
Observe the movement of the forest & water.
Breathe the aroma of the air, water, plants and forest.
Feel the texture of the air, water, trees and plants.
Listening to the sound of air, water, critters & birds;
Taste the air of the breezes or soothing snacks.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.

description:
Awakening Asheville
**What if one evening could remind you what it feels like to be fully human, together?**

**What is Spirited Improv Playshop?**

A 2-hour playshop of movement, music, story, and unscripted connection. No script, no performance pressure, no experience needed. Just a circle of people willing to show up, play, and see what unfolds when a room lets go of the need to get it right.

**Who it's for**
People craving real connection, creative expression, and a little more Love in their lives. If you're drawn to personal growth, spiritual community, or simply want an evening that feels different from the ones that came before it, this is for you.

**Led by**
Jessica Chilton, an expressive arts practitioner and TEDx performer with twenty years in improvisational performing arts. She holds space with warmth and a deep trust in whatever wants to emerge in the room.

What people are saying
"It's like free-falling into the unknown, but with a big, warm, and fluffy safety net that hugs you when you land."

"We're just taking off all our stuff and walking out in our essence."

Come see for yourself.

Register at spiritedimprov.com for $40.

Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom
Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. 
Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! 
Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

title: Hawkwatch at Grandfather Mountain
description:
Hawkwatch at Grandfather Mountain
with Lauren Lampley 
Wednesday, September 16  |  9 am – 3 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Ever wonder where our migratory hawks go in the wintertime? Join Arboretum and Grandfather Mountain staff on a day filled with scanning the skies for these migratory birds. There is a chance to see hundreds of migratory hawks as they fly by the mountain on their way south for the winter. During this day we will also talk about the different types of hawks and other birds of prey that migrate following the Appalachian Mountains. 
This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. If you prefer to meet us there, you will want to let us know and we will tell you where to meet.  
This program will take place outside and will follow rocky paths onto the Linville Peak area. Those uncomfortable with crossing the bridge can set up a chair on the building side of the bridge but would not be present for the main counting. Bring your own chair or cushion to sit on the rocks and your binoculars or spotting scope if you have one. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time with no shade. Bring a lunch and/or snacks or plan to leave the group to purchase food from Mildred’s Grill located at the Museum down the mountain a bit. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

title: The Flame Within
description:
Awakening Asheville
A weekly Wednesday morning circle for spiritual kinksters, sensual seekers, witches, lovers, shadow-workers, and the kink-curious who want to explore the deeper layers beneath desire.
This is a space for the parts of us that don’t always fit neatly into everyday life: the sacred, the sexual, the curious, the complicated, the powerful, the tender, the hungry, the healing, the hidden.

$20 RSVP Strongly suggested [at this link](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSezke4QJf6Vdwt0y3Di08XxMizntChymmHLCxMBOpf8xCApiA/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=109188294329093739010).

Each week offers a different doorway into self-knowledge and embodied exploration, such as:
✦ Desire and erotic self-discovery
✦ Shadow work and shame alchemy
✦ Tarot, oracle, magick, and divination
✦ Sensual journaling and self-expression
✦ Moon rituals and symbolic practice
✦ Body wisdom and nervous system awareness
✦ Kink-informed conversations around power, consent, and boundaries
✦ Brave intimacy, vulnerability, and communication

This is an all-gender, 18+, clothed, facilitated, consent-centered circle. All orientations, relationship structures, identities, and experience levels are welcome.

You are welcome to share deeply, lightly, or not at all.

Bring your curiosity. Bring your contradictions. Bring the self you’re still learning how to claim.

Coffee and tea provided. Bring your own mug.

title: Arbor Evenings - NC Arboretum 🌿🎶
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
## Arbor Evenings at the NC Arboretum 🌿🎶

Come spend an evening with AVL Digital Nomads at the **North Carolina Arboretum for Arbor Evenings**. We’ll wander the gardens, grab a drink, listen to live music, and enjoy golden hour with fellow Nomads.
**Arbor Evenings is free to attend**, and we have **10 complimentary parking passes** for our group. Since parking is normally $20 per vehicle, we’re going to carpool and make those passes go as far as possible.

### IMPORTANT: Where We’re Meeting

**Do not go directly to the Arboretum if you plan to use one of our complimentary passes.**
We’ll meet at:
**the "At Home" store parking lot**
980 Brevard Rd
Asheville, NC 28806
Meet **behind Chick-fil-A** and look for cars with **AVL Digital Nomads signs on top**. We’ll organize carpools there and head to the Arboretum together.

### Have an Arboretum Membership?

Even better. **If you already have an Arboretum membership/pass and are willing to drive and carpool other Nomads, please let us know in the Meetup comments.** Your vehicle can enter free, which allows us to save our complimentary passes for other members.

### A Few Things to Know

* Arbor Evenings itself is **free**
* AVLDN has **10 complimentary parking passes**
* We’ll distribute those through our carpools
* After our complimentary passes are claimed, parking is **$20 per vehicle**
* Arboretum members who receive free entry/parking are encouraged to drive and help us carpool
* Food and beverages are available for purchase at the event

Let's get away from the screen, discover a gem of Asheville, meet some people you might not otherwise cross paths with, and enjoy a beautiful evening outside.
Remote work gives us freedom. **Community still requires showing up.**
Come hang out with us. 🌿
**More about Arbor Evenings:**
[NC Arboretum Arbor Evenings](https://ncarboretum.org/arborevenings/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title: Shut Up & Write!® in Hendersonville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:** This event is moving to the Shut Up & Write! website. To RSVP to upcoming session or connect with other local writers, [join the new group page here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2x848mVGaJ ).

If you have any questions, feel free to [reach out here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/contact).

Thanks!
The Shut Up & Write! Team

\-\-\-

Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

When you show up, say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once you’re all settled, take some time to chat with your fellow writers. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

**A note about the format**
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://www.shutupwrite.com).

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: 🌟 Beyond Gender: Our Divine Heritage & Sri Rudram Mantra Recital
description:
Center for Spiritual Living Asheville
**🌟 Wed Nite Special - Beyond Gender: Our Divine Heritage**
**& Sri Rudram Mantra Recital**

🗓 Wednesday, September 16
🕡 6:30 PM
💝 Value-Based Donation

Join us for an inspiring evening with Kenneth Douglas as he explores timeless spiritual wisdom through an engaging presentation and a powerful mantra recital.

**🌿 Beyond Gender: Our Divine Heritage**
In today's world, conversations about gender can often become divisive. Kenneth offers a fresh and deeply spiritual perspective by exploring the Divine Masculine and Divine Feminine as sacred energies that exist within every person—not merely as identities, but as universal principles that shape our lives.

✨ Through a beautifully illustrated presentation, you'll discover:
🔹 A deeper understanding of Divine Masculine and Divine Feminine energies
🔹 How imbalance within these energies influences individuals and society
🔹 A spiritual framework for healing, harmony, and inner clarity
🔹 Practical insights for living with greater balance and purpose

**🕉 Sri Rudram Mantra Recital**
Experience the profound vibration of one of the world's most revered Vedic mantras.
Traditionally chanted for protection, purification, and the removal of obstacles, the Sri Rudram is more than a performance—it's a spiritual discipline. Kenneth introduces the mantra with thoughtful context before leading a live recital that invites peace, presence, and deep stillness.

**🎶 During this sacred experience you'll enjoy:**
🔸 A brief introduction to the meaning and tradition of Sri Rudram
🔸 The calming rhythm and repetition of this ancient Vedic chant
🔸 A space for quiet reflection and inner renewal
🔸 An opportunity to experience sacred sound in community

**👤 About Kenneth Douglas**
Kenneth Douglas is a seasoned speaker, content creator, and U.S. Marine veteran whose life journey spans global service, spiritual awakening, mentoring, music, meditation, fatherhood, and community leadership. Drawing from decades of lived experience, he inspires others to navigate life's challenges with greater clarity, resilience, and purpose.
Whether you're curious about spiritual philosophy, seeking greater inner balance, or simply longing for an evening of meaningful reflection and sacred sound, this promises to be a memorable and enriching experience.
We look forward to sharing this special evening with you! 💜

Self-Care and Community of Practice Led by Black Facilitators, for the Black Community.

About this Event
"Caring for myself is not self - indulgence; it is self-preservation, and that is an act of political warfare." Audre Lorde

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! (We offer a parallel session for Allies to connect, learn and find support in their work to dismantle racism at allies.eventbrite.com)

We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

This 1-Hour Restorative Session Includes:
-Open, safe space for sharing and self-care for Black people
-Facilitated discussion
-Breath work and meditation

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.
Unleash the Hidden Healing Power of the Breath
-SKY Schools

title: Grandfather Mtn; a challenge.
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
We are the **Sloth Hike Team of WNC**: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t ***!!***
**John Muir didn’t like the word ‘hike’. *“We ought to saunter through them reverently, not 'hike' through them.”***
I am going to Grandfather Mtn Park; Up to 8 ppl are welcome to join me.
**Hike Distance: 2.0 mi total Accum ascent: 400 ft; Elevation: 5000 ft.** Trail map in photos below.
Pace: **1.0mph – because I’m an ol’ Codger.**
**Difficulty: All of the trail is large rock - most is climbing.**
**Masticating will be ‘in motion’.**
Drive time: 1.5 hrs/ 77 mi 1-way. (arrive 10am)
**Return Not earlier than: 2:30p (=6.0 hrs)**
***Carpool contributions appreciated. $10.00 suggested***
***Park Admission Fee: $30 per person.***
Weather Check: Blowing Rock, NC
https://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Grandfather-Mountain/forecasts/latest
Weather cancellations will be posted the evening before.
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 3 driver(s) (=12ppl)
We suggest slightly open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
**I do *NOT* suggest bringing Fluffy on this event**
**DESCRIPTION;**
Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have challenging surprises.
Mountain Trolls are thieves; Zip your backpacks tight.
We will park at the Hikers Parking area and hike the Grandfather Ext trail (0.6mi) to the Grandfather Trail (0.5mi) to the Swinging bridge. Then returned on the 'Bridge trail' (0.4mi). **Several steep sections (400 ft accum ascent).** All of the trail is large rock - most is climbing.
**The Bridge Trail:** walk through rhododendron, galax, red spruce, Fraser fir, and yellow birch. 0.4 mile on switchbacks down the mountain, passing under the Swinging Bridge. You'll be awed by the massive rock outcroppings on this trail.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.

title: Geology of the Blue Ridge Field Class
description:
Geology of the Blue Ridge Field Class
with Anton DuMars 
Thursday, September 17  |  11am – 5pm 
BRN – Core 
Register Here!
  
On this Field Experience, we will observe and interpret evidence of Appalachian mountain-building events. Participants can put their hands on a 380+/- million-year-old pluton and observe their post-uplift weathering, jointing, and exfoliation. In addition, participants observe and interpret river processes, transport, and depositional environments of sediments derived from up-gradient sources. The experience includes on-site geologic map reading and interpretation. 
This off-site program has stops in the Pisgah Forest near Brevard NC along The Pisgah Highway including Daniel Ridge and the Davidson River. 
This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. If you prefer to meet us there, you will want to let us know and we will tell you where to meet.  
This program will take place outside and will follow easy to moderate trails. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Anton DuMars, a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. Ideally, he’s spending time on a hiking trail or aboard his sailboat.

title: Tour des Trees
description:
Tour des Trees
September 17, 2026 from 2 pm to 4:30 pm
Tree Research and Education Endowment Fund (TREE Fund) in celebration of the end of the week-long bike ride, the Tour des Trees, has partnered with the North Carolina Arboretum to create a Community Day event where locals can learn more about trees and urban forests. 
Events will kick-off with an “Ask an Arborist” session from 2-3pm at the Education Center, where people can learn about how to take care of the trees on their property and ask questions to arborists about how to keep their trees healthy and strong. At 2:15, Mycology students from UNC-Asheville will lead Mushroom Walks throughout the grounds. At 3:45, children can learn all about why trees are important and how they grow by attending a PEP Rally featuring author and YouTube star, Professor Elwood Pricklethorn. 
Professor Pricklethorn’s presentations are perfect for grade school children that want to learn more about trees in an exciting and sometimes comical way. He will also be visiting three different elementary schools during the week in western North Carolina, as a part of the Tour des Trees’ outreach events. “We are looking forward to ending this year’s ride in Asheville and we are very pleased to be able to work with the North Carolina Arboretum on these events where we can help grow the knowledge of local residents about the importance of tree research,” said Jonathan Cain, Communication and Engagement Manager at TREE Fund. “An important part of this ride and the reason why our riders join us year in and year out is because we are able to get out into the communities we ride through and talk trees.” The Tour des Trees bike ride is a week-long ride that takes place in different locations every year with riders traveling in from all over the world. This year, 95 riders will participate. “Asheville will be a wonderful city to end this year’s ride and having a place like the North Carolina Arboretum in town where we can interact with people that appreciate being outside and appreciate trees is a great way to cap off the week,” said Cain. 
More information on where the riders will be going and the events throughout the week at TREE Fund’s website, www.treefund.org. 
These programs will take place in the Auditorium within the Education Center.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ledford Gap/Powhatan Loop: 7 mi., 1,100 ft. elev.
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**[RSVP opens Sunday, Sept. 13th, 8:00 pm]**

With so many trail segments cobbled together, this is practically a grand tour of the Bent Creek area! We'll start at the Ledford Branch parking lot and cover parts of Bent Creek Gap Rd., Explorer Loop Trail, Sleepy Gap Trail, Shut-in Trail, Deerfield Connector, Small Creek Trail, Homestead Trail, Hard Times Rd., and Deer Lake Lodge Trail. (There are a few other unnamed segments as well.) Total distance is around 6.5 miles with an elevation gain of just under 1,100'. We'll do a moderate pace of around 2.4 mph. It's not an easy hike for many of us. I'd give it a 4 out of 10, while many of my other hikes are in the 2 - 3.5 range with half the elevation gain.

Wear sensible hiking footwear, and bring an ample water supply. Around 2/3 of the way through, we'll find a spot for a short snack break.

***Dog Policy:*** Dogs are extremely welcome but must be leashed.

***Guest Policy:*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they should join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, contact me in advance and ask if it's okay to bring a "+1" after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, I MAY be able to add your guest.

**MEET-UP TIME AND PLACE**
Please arrive at the Ledford Branch parking lot a few minutes early for sign-in and introductions. It may be busy, so leave some extra time in case you need to park along the access road and walk to the lot. We'll hit the trail a.s.a.p. after 9:00 AM.

**DIRECTIONS**
From Exit 33 on I-26,
Head south on Brevard Rd. (Rt. 191) for 2 miles
Right at the lights on Bent Creek Ranch Rd.
After .3 miles bear left onto Wesley Branch Rd.
Go about 2 miles, past Rice Pinnacle and Hard Times Trailheads
Bear right at the fork & the sign for Ledford Branch Trailhead.
Go around 500' to the parking lot on the right.

**[Google Maps link](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HjbbgfJryKjeHLJ4A)**

**COURTESY TO WAIT-LISTERS (Please abide!)**
Only sign up if you \*TRULY\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers will have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.
If you're on the waiting list, keep checking the evening before. Despite what I wrote above, we always get last-minute dropouts.

**WEATHER**
I'll monitor National Weather Service forecasts for the hike area and email cancellation messages by 7:30 AM if the forecast is for more than a 50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
If you have any questions, message me through MeetUp until 8:00 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy on the trail, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: (803) 767-3094.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-
**LEGALESE**
This Asheville Hiking Group event involves hiking and, possibly, transportation to and from the meetup site. Participants are responsible for their own safety and, by joining a hike, affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Hiking may involve risks to oneself and property. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can eliminate all risks or be responsible for your well-being. Participants assume full responsibility for any injuries, damages, or losses.

title: How Plants Grow: A Close Look at Plant Growth and Structures
description:
How Plants Grow: A Close Look at Plant Growth and Structures
with Alexandra Holland 
Friday, September 18  |  1 – 2:30pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Building on Beginning Botany, this class examines the variety of plant cells and tissues, how they are organized to support plant functions, and how they mature as a plant grows. We’ll explore the structural similarities and differences between plants as small as a trout lily and as large as a white oak.  Prerequisite:  Beginning Botany 
Alexandra Holland has a passion for getting people excited about the natural world through classes, hikes, and photography.  She graduated from Duke University and earned her master’s degree in botany from the University of Texas at Austin.  While in Texas, Alexandra managed the UTEX Culture Collection of Algae at UT Austin and volunteered with education programs at the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center.  Upon moving to Asheville, she began volunteering with the NC Arboretum’s youth education programs.  In 2008 she was in the first class of students to be certified as Blue Ridge Naturalists.   Alexandra teaches botany classes at the NC Arboretum and leads nature hikes in Western NC for groups of all ages.

title: Landscape Design Fundamentals (2-sessions)
description:
Landscape Design Fundamentals (2-sessions)
with Jennifer Verprauskus 
Friday, September 18  |  1 – 3:30pm 
Friday, September 25  |  1 – 3:30pm 
BREG – Core 
Register Here!
  
Students will learn the fundamentals of landscape design in a two-part class that introduces participants to design principles, site assessment and planning, among other topics. Gain a better understanding of what comes into play in creating and managing sustainable and aesthetically appealing landscapes. We will also brush on some basic permaculture design practices. You will come away empowered to be more creative, instinctive, decisive and purposeful in understanding good design and more adept at recognizing what’s not. 
Jennifer Verprauskus is a North Carolina Licensed Landscape Architect and a Permaculture Design Certificate Holder. She studied Landscape Architecture at the University of Massachusetts & Cal Poly. Since graduating, she has traveled the world to help people grow trees and their own food. She is the founder of both UpBeet Landscapes and BareRoot Designs, PLLC.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Sep 18th Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space. use the link below to reserve your tickethttps://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/sep-18-community-cuddle

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**

1. Clothes stay on for the whole event.
2. You do not have to touch anyone at this event.
3. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone.
4. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with.
5. Speak up if you have a question, concern, or if you need assistance with anything during the event.
6. All emotions are welcome- we love vulnerability.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

\*ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.

* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
\*BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

Evening Dance Wave 7:00 pm \- 9:00 pm \| Warmup 7pm \| Opening Circle 7:30pm

Intention: Rise Up!

Individuals and communities throughout the world find themselves on the vulnerable end of a conflict yet find the determination to rise up through civil action, protest, song, art, kindness, and mutual support. What creates the strength of will to move beyond the freeze response in order to create change? This dance honors of the people of the world who transcend the fear and uncertainty and take action toward a more just and kinder planet.

description:

Two young lovers from feuding families fall head over heels, hoping their secret romance will bring peace to Verona. But family pride and fate have other plans. Stepped ground seating is free, remember to bring blankets, pillows, campchairs, etc to be more comfortable. If you’d like to make an online donation before the show you can do so here: [https://www.montfordparkplayers.org/](https://www.montfordparkplayers.org/get-tickets-2/)

The actors will come around at intermission for cash or venmo donations and they typically have a food and drink vendor of some kind.

title: Biltmore Estate: Walk the Westover Black Trails
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Located at The Inn on Biltmore Estate, the Westover Black Trails provide access to some of Biltmore's beautiful woodlands. We will loop the Black Trail in a counterclockwise direction.

Biltmore says it is 3.5 miles. The Black Trail is narrow. It is a moderately difficult trail. There is elevation change, but just a bit strenuous. (For those who have walked the Green and Blue Trails, there is less chance for confusion.)

When you drive to the Inn, you will turn onto its access road. Near the entrance to the Inn is the entrance to the parking area. There are two rows of parking, an upper row closer to the Inn, and a lower row a little further from the Inn. We will gather on the lower row at the far end (away from the Inn).

If you need a restroom prior to the walk, Antler Hill is very close and there are public restrooms there. No restroom facilities are available during the walk.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case you will want light hiking boots. Walking sticks are desirable; I plan to use two. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome if they are accustomed to trail walking. Trail strollers would find this a bit difficult.

There is a grounds admission fee. We walk at Biltmore several times each year, so an annual grounds pass is highly recommended.

Many regular Biltmore guests have never walked the Westover Trails. I think you will enjoy these.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: The Art of Wellbeing: Therapeutic Art Making in the Museum
description:
Art has the power to heal, restore, and reconnect us to what matters most. Join us at the Asheville Art Museum for a guided art-making session led by a registered art therapist, designed to explore how art can be a tool to nurture your mental and emotional wellbeing. Whether you’re a seasoned artist or have never picked up a paintbrush, come as you are and leave feeling refreshed. Join Alexis for sessions on August 15, September 19, and December 19. 
Dr. C. Alexis Decosimo is a licensed mental health clinician, registered art therapist, and Doctor of Public Health. She specializes in helping children, families, and individuals access healing through blending therapeutic artmaking and evidence-based approaches including EMDR, cognitive behavioral therapy, and person-centered approaches.
She believes in meeting clients where they are, drawing on creative modalities to open pathways to healing that talk therapy alone may not reach. Her clinical work is deeply informed by over a decade of international experience building mental health programs in some of the world’s most under-resourced settings, giving her a grounded, adaptive, and culturally sensitive approach to care.
In her Asheville practice, she brings that same commitment to accessible, ethical, and community-rooted mental health support to help clients process trauma, build resilience, and find their footing through the power of expressive therapy.   For more information follow: Ashevillearttherapy.com

title: Reptiles of Western North Carolina
description:
Reptiles of Western North Carolina
with Carlton Burke 
Saturday, September 19  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
Register Here!
  
The Southern Appalachian Mountain region hosts an interesting combination of cold-blooded reptiles, based largely on various factors such as the diverse mountain elevations and the unique forest and other habitat types. Species here range from the endangered and threatened Bog Turtle and Timber Rattlesnake to more common species such as the Black Rat Snake and Northern Fence Lizard. Participants in this class will learn about the various reptile species in western North Carolina, their life cycles and habitats, and threats and conservation efforts in place to protect them. In addition, some live mountain reptiles will be joining us as special guests. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: Book + Art | Fiction and Photos of Appalachia
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
September’s Book + Art lecture features an author and artist couple, Stephanie and Jeff Whetstone. Stephanie will speak about her debut novel Deep Belly of the Earth a haunting, intimate story of friendship, marriage, motherhood and the fierce pull of home set in a Kentucky coal mining community, while her husband Jeff Whetstone, Professor of Photography at Princeton, will speak about his latest collection of photographs of Appalachia, including the one on the cover of Deep Belly of the Earth. 
SYNOPSIS of Deep Bell of the Earth
Ava Maynard makes the difficult decision to leave her small coal mining town in Eastern Kentucky to make a life for herself and her son, Joshua, in the city. Her husband, Collis, won’t leave the mountains, even though he has been laid off from his job as a miner. When tragedy strikes, Ava reluctantly slips back into her spot in this troubled world, relying on her deepest friendships to guide her. 
Author Bio
Stephanie Whetstone earned her BA at Duke and her MFA in Creative Writing from UNC-Greensboro, where she was Fiction Editor of the Greensboro Review. She has been a fellow at Virginia Center for the Creative Arts and Hambidge, and a Peter Taylor Scholar at the Sewanee Writer’s Conference. Her fiction has appeared in Tulip Tree Review, Waccamaw, Waypoints, Drafthorse, the Anthology of Appalachian Writers, and Narrative. A native of Kentucky, she now lives in Brooklyn. 
Jeff Whetstone imagines rural America through the lenses of mythology and biology. Whetstone’s work has been exhibited internationally and has received reviews in ArtForum, Art in America, the New York Times, the New Yorker, and the Los Angeles Times. Whetstone earned his MFA from the Yale School of Photography in 2001, where he received the George Sakier Prize for Photography. A recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship, as well as a fellowship from the North Carolina Arts Council, his work is in the permanent collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Nasher Museum, the Nelson Atkins Museum, the Cleveland Art Museum, the Yale Art Gallery, the New York Public Library, and the North Carolina Museum of Art. Whetstone is a Professor of the Practice of Art at Princeton University.

description:

Sunday, September 20th

Facilitator DJ SeigeA (CJ O'Reilly)

Intention: Lab & Play!

What happens when we open up to letting go of the results and seeing what happens? Let's experiment! Let's play!

## About CJ O'Reilly

CJ O'Reilly has been creating ecstatic dance waves for the Asheville community since 2014. Their eclectic mix of musical styles beckons dancers into new patterns of movement and expression through diverse time signatures and instrumentation, and a wide range of musical and emotive qualities. CJ's waves explore high peaks, beautiful vistas, juicy lowlands and the profound reflective stillness of tranquil water. CJ's dance waves are pre-produced and refined through the body and ears of a dancer and audiophile.

Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

description:
Join us for a screening of Minnie Evans: Draw or Die followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, Linda Royal. 
We are also excited that Wayne Evans, the great-grandson of Minnie Evans, who is in the documentary, will be attending the Q&A as well. 
Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit. 
Screening time: 56:10:00 
Film Synopsis: 
The film explores the inspirational life and artistic mastery of visionary artist Minnie Evans through archived
conversations with her friend Nina Howell Starr. 
About the filmmaker: 
Linda Royal (fka Linda Booker) directed, produced, and edited the film festival award-winning
documentaries “STRAWS,” with narration by Tim Robbins, “Bringing It Home,” and “Love Lived on Death
Row.” Her films have reached audiences worldwide through film festivals, educational distribution,
community screenings, corporate offices, and in-flight entertainment. She has partnered with numerous
organizations for grassroots advocacy and impact campaigns. Linda was the Director of Operations for
the Sonoma International Film Festival in 2015-2016. She started By the Brook Productions after receiving
a Certificate in Documentary Studies from Duke University in 2005. Before filmmaking, Linda was an Art
Director and graphic designer for numerous publications in Florida and North Carolina.

description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

title: Autumn Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
description:
Autumn Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
with Jenne Sluder 
Tuesday, September 22 |  10 am – 4pm 
Register Here!
  
Set aside a day for quiet reflection and renewal at the North Carolina Arboretum in Asheville, centering themes from the poetry of W.S. Merwin. Calm your mind, refresh your spirit, and relax your body and nervous system with a gentle immersion into mind-body centering practices both indoors and in nature. Expect slow, mindful yoga and qigong, guided meditation, progressive relaxation + sound bath, contemplative readings from W.S. Merwin, and time for personal journaling and quiet time in nature. All mind-body practices will be gentle and accessible, including the choice to do any seated movements or meditations in a chair or on a cushion according to your own body’s needs. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions. 
●  See a full listing of Adult Education Programs at the North Carolina Arboretum here! Questions? Check our FAQs. 
●  We are committed to fostering a diverse, supportive learning community. If the cost of a class is a barrier for you, please complete this scholarship form and we will see what kind of assistance we can provide.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: Sapphic Book Club!  - July
description:
Queers to the Front!
Our book club read for September is *Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil* by V.E. Schwab.

*This is a story about hunger.*

**1532\. Santo Domingo de la Calzada\.**
A young girl grows up wild and wily—her beauty is only outmatched by her dreams of escape. But María knows she can only ever be a prize, or a pawn, in the games played by men. When an alluring stranger offers an alternate path, María makes a desperate choice. She vows to have no regrets.

*This is a story about love.*
**1827\. London\.**
A young woman lives an idyllic but cloistered life on her family’s estate, until a moment of forbidden intimacy sees her shipped off to London. Charlotte’s tender heart and seemingly impossible wishes are swept away by an invitation from a beautiful widow—but the price of freedom is higher than she could have imagined.

*This is a story about rage.*
**2019\. Boston\.**
College was supposed to be her chance to be someone new. That’s why Alice moved halfway across the world, leaving her old life behind. But after an out-of-character one-night stand leaves her questioning her past, her present, and her future, Alice throws herself into the hunt for answers . . . and revenge.

***This is a story about life—***
***how it ends, and how it starts.***

title: Long-term Effects of Hurricane Helene on Southern Appalachian Ecosystems
description:
Long-term Effects of Hurricane Helene on Southern Appalachian Ecosystems
with Dan Lazar 
Wednesday, September 23  |  1 pm – 3 pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
It has been two years since hurricane Helene ravaged the ecosystems of Western North Carolina, uprooting trees and causing major flooding along mountain rivers and streams. How have the animals and plants of the affected areas responded to this historic event?  Where do songbirds go to escape hurricane winds?  How can fish and aquatic invertebrates tolerate such massive flooding?  What factors determine which trees are toppled and which survive?  We will investigate the long-term effects of Hurricane Helene on the natural plant and animal communities of Western North Carolina during this illustrated lecture followed by a short walk on Arboretum grounds to observe the ongoing recovery of hurricane-damaged areas. 
Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.
