title: Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops
description:
Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops
with Mark Dempsey 
Thursday, September 24  |  1 pm – 4 pm 
BREG – Soil Health Core 
Register Here!
  
Come learn about how soil works and how to improve soil health. We will cover the basics of soil, the critical role of organic matter, how to sample soil and interpret a nutrient test, and what actions you can take to make your soil better. Drawing from research and on-farm experience, the class emphasizes practical, science-based strategies for improving soil health, reducing erosion, and building resilient farming systems. 
Mark Dempsey works with the Carolina Farm Stewardship Association as conservation specialist and soil health educator. His background includes more than 15 years of research and education in soil microbiology, no-till farming, cover crops, and sustainable agriculture systems. He teaches practical, science-based approaches to improving soil health, soil function, and long-term farm resilience.

title: Free Live Music: Jvnk Drawer
description:
Some bands write songs. Jvnk Drawer excavates them
— pulling from a thirty-year vein of half-forgotten gems, salvaged riffs, and songs that were simply waiting for the right band to play them. The result is alternative rock with real mileage on it: melodies sharp enough to catch you off guard, lyrics honest enough to stick. 
At its center is Gavin Conner, a songwriter whose Asheville roots run back to 2007, when he arrived in town to join local favorites, If You Wannas. What followed was a long apprenticeship in the local scene — a solo run, countless stages, and a songbook that quietly grew into something few writers ever amass. By 2017, that songbook needed a band worthy of it, and Jvnk Drawer was born, with drummer Chris Peterson and bassist Erik Avots rounding out the lineup and giving the songs a pulse. 
Like most everything else, the band’s momentum stalled when the pandemic hit, and the members drifted toward other projects to wait it out. But the songs didn’t go anywhere, and neither did the itch to play them. Jvnk Drawer has since reformed sharper and more locked-in than ever, splicing decades of Gavin’s back catalog together with newly written material that sounds like it’s always belonged there. 
The name says it best: a jumble of pieces that when put together, somehow make perfect sense. Equal parts catchy and cutting, Jvnk Drawer is proof that the best songs are worth digging for. 
Gavin Conner — Vocals, Guitar Chris Peterson — Drums Erik Avots — Bass 
  
Free Show 6-8p. All Ages.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Walking Meditation & Qigong
description:
Walking Meditation & Qigong
with Jenne Sluder 
Friday, September 25  |  9 – 10am 
Register Here!
  
Enjoy a slow, mindful walking meditation through the gardens, practicing breath awareness and sensory attention to touch the deep peace and simple wonders of quiet time in nature. This session begins with a series of gentle and easy Qigong movements to clear the mind, release tension, support the body and brain’s natural healing processes, and generate a sense of inner calm. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Bats of the NC Arboretum with Mist Netting Demonstration
description:
Bats of the NC Arboretum with Mist Netting Demonstration
with Megan Zeger and team 
Friday, September 25  |  7 – 9pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
The NC Arboretum hosts a variety of bat species in our forests. Join a group of biologists for a presentation about the recent acoustic bat study they conducted on the Arboretum’s property this summer and which species they found. Then, once the presentation is over, join the crew out in the woods for a mist netting demonstration if weather allows. During this class, you will learn all about the different species of bats that call the NC Arboretum home, how biologists collect data about bat presence in a location using microphones, and even might have the chance to see live, wild bats up close and personal! 
Participants will not be handling the bats, and the bats will only be handled by the trained biologists. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Megan Zeger is a graduate student at Virginia Tech studying four imperiled bat species in the Asheville, NC area. She has been studying and working with wildlife in the southern Appalachians since 2018 when she started her undergraduate program in wildlife conservation. She has been working with bats since 2022 and has done research on various species in Maryland, North Carolina, Utah, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wyoming. 
Jessica Davey is a wildlife biologist currently working for Virginia Tech’s Conservation and Management Institute. Having graduated from Lees-McRae College in 2021, she has since worked primarily as a bat researcher in six different states. Her experience ranges from Mist netting and acoustic surveys to conducting hibernacula and white-nose swabbing in the caves of Florida. She hopes to continue gaining as much knowledge as she can about the world’s only flying mammal. 
Katie Kadkovsky is a recent Biology graduate from UNC-Chapel Hill. While there, she worked in molecular biology labs at Chapel Hill and Duke studying fungi. Katie was introduced to the bat world at UNC-CH via acoustic surveys of NC’s sky islands. Currently, she is a wildlife biologist with Virginia Tech CMI helping characterize the presence of tri-colored bats in the greater Asheville area to support conservation practices. 
Liam Jawish is a recent graduate from Virginia Tech! He is currently working as a wildlife biologist surveying bats in Asheville, NC. He previously worked on Jaguar surveys in Belize, CA, and bear work in central Virginia. 
Lucy Kraus is a wildlife biologist with the Conservation Management Institute at Virginia Tech. She graduated from UNC-Chapel Hill in 2026 with a degree in environmental science. In the past, she has worked in prescribed fire and environmental education.

title: Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan
location: Baker Exhibit Center
description:
Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan
September 26, 2026 – January 10, 2027
Baker Exhibit Hall
“Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan” features Ronan Donovan’s stunning images and videos of wild wolves in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem and Ellesmere Island in the high Canadian Arctic. Since 2014, National Geographic Explorer and photographer Ronan Donovan has examined the relationship between wild wolves and humans in order to better understand the animals, our shared history, and what drives the persistent human-wolf conflict. 
The exhibition, created by National Geographic Society and the National Museum of Wildlife Art, will display images and videos—highlighting the contrast between wolves that live in perceived competition with humans and wolves that live without human intervention.“Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan” will introduce visitors to the daily lives of wolves in the Arctic—how they hunt, play, travel, and rest in one of the harshest environments on Earth—with unparalleled intimacy. 
About Ronan Donavan
A field biologist turned conservation photographer and filmmaker, Ronan Donovan has explored the human relationship to nature and wildlife on all seven continents. Donovan’s passion for conserving wild animals and wild places was ignited as a child growing up in Vermont and later during his years as a wildlife field biologist researching spotted owls and chimpanzees. He transitioned to visual storytelling as a way to amplify the wildlife researchers and conservationists that Donovan collaborated with. In addition to his National Geographic work on wolves, Donovan has documented human-chimpanzee conflicts in Uganda, and the legacy work of primatologist Dian Fossey focused on mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda. Donovan strives to reconnect viewers to the natural world through the lives of our fellow social mammals to highlight our shared past and interwoven future.

We will hear from Adam Warwick, Stewardship Manager for The Nature Conservancy, on the role and importance of fire in our region. This will be followed by a networking event with local natural resource professionals to learn more about job opportunities, funding, technical assistance and other available resources. A free lunch will be provided, followed by a tour of a burn unit on the Warren Wilson College Forest with Dr. Armin Weise, Assistant Professor of Forest Management at Western Carolina University, and Juniper Odell, Prescribed Fire Specialist with the Nature Conservancy. They will be leading a discussion on the ecology of the site and how to properly conduct a controlled burn. The event will be held in 110 Boon Hall and will begin at 9:00am. The event is free.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Wellness Day
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Wellness Day at the Asheville Art Museum 
The Asheville Art Museum’s Wellness Day invites visitors to experience the museum as a place for restoration, reflection, creativity, and community. Throughout the day, guests are encouraged to slow down and engage with art through a series of thoughtfully curated wellness experiences that nurture both mind and body. 
Afternoon Tea Parlor | Windgate Foundation Atrium and Plaza noon–4pm 
Yoga on the Plaza | 12:30–1pm 
 Yoga in the Galleries | 1:30–2pm 
Live Music: Soothing sounds in the Galleries and the Windgate Foundation Atrium | noon–4pm 
Drop-in Workshop: Therapeutic Art Making | John & Robyn Horn Education Center (level 3) 1–4pm 
Slow Art Tours | 11:30–noon, 1–1:30pm, 2:30–3pm 
RESERVE TICKETS NOW 
Museums are uniquely positioned to serve as spaces for wellness. Unlike many public environments, museums invite contemplation, curiosity, and intentional looking. They provide settings where individuals can step away from daily demands and immerse themselves in experiences that inspire wonder, empathy, and personal discovery. Art has the power to help people process emotions, spark meaningful conversations, and connect across diverse perspectives and lived experiences. 
By integrating mindfulness, movement, creative expression, and music into the museum experience, Wellness Day expands the role of the Asheville Art Museum as a community resource dedicated not only to the appreciation of art but also to the holistic well-being of those it serves. The program demonstrates that museums can be active partners in fostering healthier, more connected communities by creating welcoming spaces where creativity becomes a pathway to healing, resilience, and joy.

title: Fall Tree ID
description:
Fall Tree ID
With Lauren Lampley 
Friday, September 26  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Join this class as we discuss how to use different characteristics and field guides to identify common trees of Western North Carolina found here at the NC Arboretum. We will look at using different characteristics including habitat, bark, buds, growth pattern, leaf shape, and fruit/nut shape to identify trees. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

What do we pay when we pay attention?

Ted is interested in anything that can get him out of his head, and music and movement do a pretty good job of that. He hopes to offer music that facilitates an inner journey and invitations that create a shift. [Get Your Tickets Here](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/witchy-ways-day-retreat-tickets-1996341264462)
**Calling in all healers, plant parents, mothers, artists, mystics, rebels, and seekers.**
This day is an invitation to remember and return to all that you are.

Together, we’ll spend an autumn afternoon slowing down, dropping in, and reconnecting with ourselves, the season, and one another through ritual, reflection, movement, and a little witchcraft.

As we move through the energies of fall, we’ll explore the seasonal invitation to both release what has run its course and intentionally call in what we’re ready to cultivate next.

**Flow of the Day**
*We’ll begin by gathering in opening circle, setting our intentions, calling in the directions, and grounding into the space through a guided meditation and energetic release.*

*From there, we’ll move into a ceremonial teaching and transmission, exploring the astrological energies of Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius alongside sacred feminine archetypes that can support us through the shifting season. Guided journaling, shadow reflection, and group sharing will offer space to bring these teachings into your own lived experience.*

*After a nourishing snack break, we’ll return to the body through intentional yoga and movement, creating space for integration and embodiment.*

*We’ll close our time together with a seasonal ritual. A little autumn witchcraft devoted to releasing what you’re ready to leave behind and calling in what you desire to cultivate. Through apple magic, fire, candlelight, and intention, you’ll create a ritual piece to take home and continue tending throughout the season.*

*Our gathering will conclude with a closing prayer and circle, sealing the magic of the day and honoring what has shifted, opened, or been remembered. Snacks and tea will be served.*

**About your guides**
**Jenn (She/Her)** is an intuitive healer trained Yoga Teacher 9+ years, Reiki Master, Astrologer and Spiritual Coach. She combines her knowledge of the body from 13 years working in physical therapy with all spiritual tools that have contributed to her own healing & spiritual journey to help guide others.
**Vi (They/Them)** is a practicing Witch & Psychic who is a trained Yoga Teacher, Reiki Master, and Tarot Reader. They combine their passions of astrology, divination, dance, and creative expression to help others listen to their intuition.
**Alessandra Mary (she/her)** is a ceremonialist, Akashic priestess, mystic, author, and sacred storyteller devoted to the path of remembrance. Through sacred gatherings and oracular transmissions, she weaves soulful experiences that invite you into deeper connection with synchronicity, authenticity, and the unseen magic woven through everyday life. She stewards the land we will be gathering on.

description:
Michelangelo – Love and Death offers a cinematic
journey through the great chapels and museums
of Florence, Rome and the Vatican, to the print
and drawing rooms of Europe, to explore
Michelangelo’s tempestuous life. The film goes in
search of a greater understanding of this
charismatic and enigmatic figure, both through
his relationships with his contemporaries and
his ongoing artistic legacy.
The film invites audiences to intimately examine
Michelangelo’s art and artistic process – from the
Carrara quarries where Michelangelo sourced his
marble, to the new technology being used to
attribute works. The film also offers a rare
chance to get up close to the mesmerizing
Rothschild Bronzes, which, following an
extensive research project carried out by
Academics in Cambridge in 2015, were positively
attributed to Michelangelo after over a century of debate.

title: Asheville Foodie Supper Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
🍝 Asheville Foodie Supper Club: First Stop, Italia! 🇮🇹

Sunday, September 27 | 6:00 to 9:00 PM
Strada Italiano | 27 Broadway, Downtown Asheville

Limited to 12 people

I’ve been wanting to create something a little different for Asheville Digital Nomads, something smaller, more intimate, and centered around one of my very favorite ways to bring people together. Food. 😁

So, I’m officially launching the Asheville Foodie Supper Club, a monthly culinary adventure where a small group of us will gather around a table, explore Asheville’s ridiculously good food scene, and actually have time to get to know one another.

We’re kicking this thing off with Italian. 🇮🇹🍝🍷

Our first stop is Strada Italiano in downtown Asheville, a cozy Old World-style trattoria serving regional Italian cuisine inspired by both Northern and Southern Italy. Think house-made pasta, risotto, seafood, Italian classics, good wine, and the kind of food that makes you very happy you did not stay home and eat something responsible. 😆

Each month, we’ll choose a different foodie theme. Italian one month, Korean another, Thai, Indian, Mexican, burgers, pizza, seafood, Mediterranean, tapas, and whatever other interesting culinary rabbit holes we decide to wander down.

But the food is only half the idea. The real purpose of the Asheville Foodie Supper Club is to create a different kind of social experience.

Instead of standing around at a larger event having snippets of conversations with 20 different people, we’ll sit around one table with just 8 to 12 of us. We’ll eat. We’ll talk. We’ll laugh. We’ll hear each other’s stories. We’ll linger over dinner and hopefully turn some of those people we recognize from Meetup into people we actually know.

The intention of this event is to meet interesting people, discover really good food and local restaurants, and enjoy conversations that have enough time to go somewhere.

🍷 A Little Supper Club Fine Print

This event is intentionally limited to 12 people, and unlike some of our larger gatherings, this one requires an actual restaurant reservation.

So please only RSVP if you genuinely intend to come. Don’t grab one of the 12 seats as a “maybe.” If something changes, no problem, just update your RSVP as soon as possible so someone on the waitlist has a chance to join us.

Because when there are only 12 chairs at the table, every chair matters.

Strada also offers a nice range of gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan and dairy-free options, so our first Foodie adventure should have something for just about everyone.

Come hungry and ready to connect with some fun and friendly new humans over a yummy meal together.

Welcome to the Asheville Foodie Supper Club. First stop, Italy. 🇮🇹 🍝🍷🍽️

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. title: A Call to Action with The Conservation Alliance
description:
Join us at The Mule for an evening built around community and connection, celebrating the people and organizations working to protect the land, water, and wildlife we all care about. title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

ABOUT THE MUSICIAN  
Meschiya Lake is a dynamic addition to Asheville’s music scene, bringing her powerful vocals, captivating stage presence, and genre-spanning sound to audiences across Western North Carolina. After years of building an acclaimed career in New Orleans, Lake has made Asheville home, blending jazz, blues, Americana, and country influences into performances that are both timeless and fresh. Whether performing intimate originals or beloved classics, Meschiya’s heartfelt storytelling and infectious energy continue to win over local music lovers throughout the region.  
From the stages of Lincoln Center in NYC, to Brazil, Canada, Denmark, The Netherlands, Italy, Russia, the U.K., and Ireland, Meschiya Lake has shown people to express love of life through music and dance.  This passion, seemingly tireless energy, and expert skill have garnered much praise, from NPR’s top ten albums of 2010 to First Lady of Jazz 2013, at the Sun Valley Jazz Festival. But most importantly, back at home in New Orleans, Lake was recognized as Female Performer of the Year, three years running, at the Big Easy Awards, was named Best Female Singer in Offbeat Magazine’s Best of the Beat poll in 2013 and 2014.  
For more information on Meschiya Lake please visit  www.meschiyalake.com

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Fall Tree ID
description:
Fall Tree ID
With Hannah Lilly and Ben Warfield 
Friday, October 2  |  1pm – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Join this group as we talk about how to identify the trees of Western North Carolina as they start to lose their leaves. Many of our native species are identifiable even when they’re dormant, and learning this practice is a rewarding and useful skill for all naturalists. We will talk about how to use the bark, twigs, and more to be able to recognize new and familiar trees in our region. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Hannah Lilly is a Botanist and Ecologist interested in the connection between plants, people, and their environment. She studied Biology with a concentration in Ecology, Evolution, and the Environment (BS) at Appalachian State University. She has since worked for the North Carolina and Virginia Natural Heritage Programs conducting field work to monitor rare and sensitive plant species, and to help conserve the truly special natural communities of The Southern Appalachians. Currently, Hannah is a Botany Technician with the US Forest Service- Pisgah in partnership with The Conservation Corps of NC, through which her understanding of WNC ecology and land management is ever growing. Hannah loves to slow down, notice the details, and revel in the whimsy of the natural world with others. 
Ben Warfield graduated from NC State University with a degree in wildlife biology, where he took many classes centered on species identification and ecosystem measurement. While at NC State, he helped teach tree identification and wildlife survey techniques during several field courses offered by the university. He currently works as a botany technician for the United States Forest Service and the Conservation Corps of North Carolina, with most of his work focused on the Pisgah National Forest.

title: Rooted & Regulated: Adaptogens and Herbal Allies for Blood Sugar, Stress & Nervous System Balance
description:
Rooted & Regulated: Adaptogens and Herbal Allies for Blood Sugar, Stress & Nervous System Balance
with Catherine Willows 
Friday, October 2  |  1 – 3:30pm 
Register Here!
  
Plants have long supported the body’s ability to adapt, regulate, and restore balance. In this class, we’ll explore how adaptogens and other plant allies can support stress resilience, nervous system regulation, and healthy blood sugar. Drawing on herbal traditions and a lifestyle medicine lens, we’ll look at how the body’s systems are deeply interconnected, and how the plant world offers gentle, effective, time-tested tools for supporting all of them. Expect an engaging blend of herbal science, traditional use, and practical takeaways — including aligned lifestyle practices — and the chance to meet some of these plants in person. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. 
While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. 
Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven  — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

On Friday October 2nd at 7 PM, Warren Wilson College celebrates the grand reopening of Kittredge Arts Center, with renowned Bluegrass act Sister Sadie headlining!  The Kittredge Arts Center grand reopening is part of the Warren Wilson College's 2026 Homecoming, and is also a homecoming for Sister Sadie's mandolinist, WWC alum' Rainy Miatke (Music Major, Class of 2025).

 

 

Tickets can be purchased here:  https://wwc-ventures.ticketspice.com/sister-sadie-and-the-kittredge-arts-center-grand-reopening 

 

For more information abuot the event, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916.  

 

 

Sister Sadie Bio:

What started as an accidental band became a force. GRAMMY-nominated. IBMA-decorated. Opry-validated. But for all the
accolades, they were often reduced to one line: an all-female bluegrass band. True—but never the point. Sister Sadie has always
been about the music. The fire. The truth.


Their new album, All Will Be Well, is that truth—loud, fearless, and free. You’ll hear echoes of bluegrass, but what rises is
something bigger: country with claws, Americana with muscle, gospel grit and raw storytelling.


From the haunting “Prodigal Daughter” to the swagger of “Do What You Want” and the aching beauty of “If I Don’t Have You,”
these six women are not performing roles—they’re telling you who they are.


This is Sister Sadie, evolved: bold, bonded, and braver than ever. They're not asking for space. They're taking it.


And they’re just getting started.

 

About Kittredge Arts Center:

Nestled within the beautiful, historic Warren Wilson College campus, the Kittredge Arts Center provides a centralized location for the arts at WWC and WNC. The Center features the 321-seat Kittredge Theater and 80-seat Williams Recital Hall, where music and performance events are featured throughout the year. Kittredge Arts Center is also available as a rental space to organizations looking for an affordable option in a beautiful location for conferences, business retreats, and other events. 

 

For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro (Assistant Professor of Music, Music Department Chair, and Director of Kittredge Arts Center) at 828-545-3916 or jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu

description:
Carson Bull is a Nashville-based singer-songwriter making waves in Americana and country music, blending deep Midwestern roots with a voice that cuts through the noise. Originally from Huntertown, Indiana, he draws on the storytelling of Bob Dylan and Waylon Jennings, the grit of Chris Stapleton, and the melodic sensibility of The Eagles to create a sound that lives at the crossroads of heartland rock and modern folk-country—timeless, honest, and distinctly his own.



His debut single “Tomorrow” (May 2025) introduced listeners to a powerful mix of gravel and grace, followed by “Better Off in Blue” (July 2025), which showcased his growing sonic range and lyrical depth. title: Bonsai in a Day: Learn, Create, Take Home
description:
Bonsai in a Day: Learn, Create, Take Home
with Rebecca Ayres 
Saturday, October 3  |  9:30 am – 4:30pm 
Register Here!
  
Although it has its roots in ancient Asian traditions, the living art of bonsai now enjoys enthusiasts throughout much of the world. This class will provide the basic concepts and skills for novices to begin growing and shaping their own miniature trees. The first half of the class will cover the fundamental horticultural and aesthetic principles of bonsai. It will include such topics as tree selection, watering, pest control, pruning, wiring, and styling. In the second half of the class, each participant will receive a pot, scissors, wire, and planting medium. With guidance from the instructor, the students will create their own bonsai to take home. Materials included in registration. 
Rebecca Ayres is a ceramic artist and gardener. A longtime Arboretum volunteer, she is the assistant to the bonsai curator and helps with overseeing the exhibition garden, the collection and the Carolina Bonsai Expo. She is a member of the Blue Ridge Bonsai Society, where she has taught workshops and classes, and is a graduate of the Arboretum’s Blue Ridge Naturalist program.

title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. 
The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. 
Join Joshua on August 22, October 3, November 7, and December 5. 
Joshua Canter is a mindfulness meditation teacher and the founder of True Nature Travels and Education, an Asheville-based organization that has offered transformative retreats and educational experiences around the world for more than 20 years. He holds a master’s degree in Contemplative Psychology and is passionate about making mindfulness accessible, grounded, and relevant to everyday life.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Adult Studio: Beginner Drop Spinning
description:
Your life is filled with textiles made from various spun threads and yarn.  Come deepen those connections with the fibers that are deeply woven into many aspects  of our lives by trying your hand at one of the earliest ways to handspin yarn using a drop spindle.  Join us for a fun, educational and meditative day of  learning the top whirl dropspindle, and maybe some other styles as welll.  We will prepare, card and spin raw wool fleece to create yarn on a drop spindle. You may have time to try different types of fibers and even different types of spindles.  You will get to take home your first handspun yarn, as well as a drop spindle  to continue exploring this new skill. 
Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with over 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the southeastern U.S., including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils.  Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.

title: Naturalist Walk and Talk - Spiders
description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk – Spiders
with Shane Myers 
Saturday, October 3  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. 
This month we will focus on the Spiders of the Arboretum. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall
description:
Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall
with Asheville Wellness Tours 
Saturday, October 3  |  2 – 5pm 
Register Here!
  
Join us for a celebration of autumn delights during this restorative afternoon nature connection retreat! From fall foliage to the monarch migration, we will immerse ourselves in the kaleidoscope that is autumn in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Enlivening our senses, calming our weary minds, and lingering in liminality. Together, we will discover natural pathways to equilibrium that will help us navigate life’s ups and downs, as well as the upcoming holiday season. 
Your guide, Kelly Bruce, will lead you on a colorful journey through the fall forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative afternoon on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience in community, enjoying a special wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Kelly Bruce is a writer, forest therapy guide and nature connection mentor based in Hendersonville, North Carolina. Her mission is to help others deepen their connection with nature, community and Self. Kelly is an Association of Nature and Forest Therapy Certified Guide and Certification Consultant. She is Wilderness First Aid and CPR certified by the American Red Cross.

ABOUT THE MUSICIAN
Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville, NC, who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. He began playing at age four and developed a strong classical foundation, later expanding into pop and musical theater. After years of studying in Spain, he now pursues music independently in the U.S., performing as a chapel pianist, choir member, and orchestra musician while also learning the organ. His cross-cultural journey shapes a deeply expressive style, with music focused on connection rather than perfection.

title: Millpond Connector at Haywood Community College on National Taco Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
As we enter Leaf Season, the temperature may indeed be cooler. Let's celebrate by going out for tacos after the walk.

To get to the Millpond Connector from our start point, we will go clockwise on the Bobcat Trail and then take the Kingfisher Trail to the Copperhead Trail. When we intersect with the Millpond Connector, we will turn left, finishing the campus loop on the Bobcat Trail. Altogether, it isn't over 2 miles. Part of the walk is on pavement, part on well-groomed trail, and part on not-as-well groomed trail. There is some small elevation change.

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring one walking stick, just in case. As always, you are urged to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have any problem. There are no bathrooms available on a Sunday afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles!

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, October 6  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**October 2026 Selection - *Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead* by Olga Tokarczuk**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Drive-Your-Plow-Over-Bones/dp/0525541330/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/51648276-drive-your-plow-over-the-bones-of-the-dead)

*In a remote Polish village, Janina devotes the dark winter days to studying astrology, translating the poetry of William Blake, and taking care of the summer homes of wealthy Warsaw residents. Her reputation as a crank and a recluse is amplified by her not-so-secret preference for the company of animals over humans. Then a neighbor, Big Foot, turns up dead. Soon other bodies are discovered, in increasingly strange circumstances. As suspicions mount, Janina inserts herself into the investigation, certain that she knows whodunit. If only anyone would pay her mind . . .*

*A deeply satisfying thriller cum fairy tale, Drive Your Plow over the Bones of the Dead is a provocative exploration of the murky borderland between sanity and madness, justice and tradition, autonomy and fate. Whom do we deem sane? it asks. Who is worthy of a voice?*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: In Conversation | An Artist Talk by Lesley Dill
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for an evening with New York-based artist Lesley Dill, whose work is featured in the current exhibition, The Art of Paper. Dill will talk about her projects that involve paper and collaboration, from huge community and large-scale installations to the intimate creation of artist books and sculptures, as well as her work with artists, poets, students, and studios, such as Tamarind and Dieu Donne.  
PAPER IS MY FRIEND:  
“Paper is about fingertip energy for me. The way one moves in to touch paper is like no other approach. It’s as if each finger has a little imaginary rocketship in it. We touch nothing else the way we touch paper. Paper is the medium of intimacy. The end result is wonder. All printmaking begins with the choice of what paper and in this way, it is about a relationship to fragility and force. This relationship comes from Poetry.”  
Bio  
Lesley Dill is an American artist working at the intersection of language and fine art in sculpture, printmaking, installation and performance, exploring the power of words to cloak and reveal the psyche. Dill has had over one hundred solo exhibitions. Her artworks are in the collections of many major museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Museum of Modern Art, New York. In 2017 she was named a fellow of The John Simon Guggenheim Foundation. Her opera, Divide Light, based on the poems of Emily Dickinson, was performed in San Jose in 2008, restaged in New York City in 2018, and captured in an award-winning film by Ed Robbins. Dill’s exhibition Wild Grace This Private Hallucinatory Moment at Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans (2025-26), a result of research conducted as a 2023-2024 Smithsonian Artist Research Fellow, examined themes of radiance and healing in seen and unseen energies. Dill’s exhibition Wilderness: Light Sizzles Around Me, organized by the Figge Art Museum and traveled to seven venues from 2021 to 2023, amplifies voices of the North American past as they wrestle with divinity, deviltry, and freedom, including Mother Ann Lee, Black Hawk, Sojourner Truth, John Brown, Emily Dickinson, Horace Pippin, and Sister Gertrude Morgan. Ms. Dill is represented by Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans. She lives and works in Brooklyn, New York. For more information and images of her work, visit www.lesleydill.net

title: Fall Garden Photography Workshop
description:
Fall Garden Photography Workshop
with Cami Calnan 
Wednesday, October 7  |  10am – 12pm 
Register Here!
  
Do you want to learn to take better seasonal fall photos in the gardens? Join us for a hands-on workshop where we use whatever camera you are working with to learn tips, tricks, and techniques to take the photos you are hoping to capture. Bring your phone, a point and shoot camera, digital SLR or film SLR camera. This class is for all levels of photographers. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Camilla Calnan is an Asheville based photographer since 2000 and has been a longtime friend and supporter of the NC Arboretum. She works to support the community and region through her photography, capturing the uniqueness that makes the Asheville area what it is. Tirelessly working to photograph nature, landscape, portrait, event, wedding, commercial/corporate, product, farm, food, restaurant, individual, and family photos, Camilla strives to fill the everchanging needs of our community.

title: Weave Kudzu Vines Into a Basket
description:
Weave Kudzu Vines Into a Basket
with Carleigh Fairchild 
Wednesday, October 7  |  10am – 4pm 
Register Here!
  
Turn wild vines into a basket in this hands-on kudzu weaving workshop. Kudzu, often thought of as an invasive plant, offers a surprising gift: strong, flexible vines that make for beautiful, functional baskets. In this workshop you’ll learn how to identify, harvest, and prepare kudzu responsibly, turning an abundant wild plant into a useful basket. Together we’ll explore weaving techniques and create baskets that reflect each of our creativity. Come away with your own handmade basket, practical knowledge for future projects, and a new appreciation for kudzu. There will be a 30 minute lunch break and materials will be provided. If you have sharp pruners, feel free to bring them along! 
Carleigh Fairchild has a deep love for the Earth. She gardens, keeps bees, wild harvests, processes animals, tans hides, weaves baskets, and finds joy in time spent around the fire. As the founder of Human Nature Connection LLC, she is dedicated to helping others rediscover respectful and collaborative relationships with the more then human world. Carleigh’s journey—including 86 days on the survival show ALONE in Patagonia—deepened her understanding of belonging and connection. With over 25 years of experience, she teaches both online and in-person classes in Western North Carolina, weaving together earth skills, community, and healing. Carleigh is also a NIASZIIH bodywork healer and instructor at Wilderness Fusion, integrating body, earth, and spirit in her practice.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.
